Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. Before we spin up a multi-week POC, procurement asked for a clear pricing path that ties the pilot credits to a committed volume if the POC converts. High-level ask: can you outline options for a short pilot (2–4 weeks) with some free credits, and then how those credits would be applied or converted if we sign a 6 or 12 month commit?

We have two primary usage patterns: bursty token generation for ad-hoc analysis and sustained embedding throughput for nightly jobs. For budgeting, our finance team needs the worst-case per-token cost and the committed tiers you’d offer.

Can you send a short options matrix (pilot-only, pilot + credit rollback on commit, and small commit w/ graduated discounts) and any standard procurement steps (MSA, SOW, DocuSign timelines)? Also flag any limitations in hosted offering for EU data residency — we may keep production in us for now.

Hi Marta — really appreciate the clear ask and the context. Below is a concise options matrix; I’ve looped in Rishi (account exec) and attached our pricing workbook so you can see per-token math. If you prefer a one-pager we can convert this into a PDF for procurement.

Summary (short):
1) Pilot-only (no commit): 100k free tokens, hosted pay-as-you-go after credits. No upfront commitment. Good for validation but no discount on post-pilot usage beyond public rates.

2) Pilot with credit conversion: 120k pilot tokens issued up front. If you sign a 6-month commit within 30 days after pilot end, up to 80% of unused pilot credits convert to a one-time usage credit applied in the first billing cycle of the committed term (applies to standard models only).

3) Small commit (recommended): 6-month commitment with monthly minimums. Commit tiers:
   - Tier A (100k/mo commit): 5% per-token discount over public hosted rate + 150k onboarding credits front-loaded
   - Tier B (300k/mo commit): 12% per-token discount + 500k onboarding credits + 1 week of paid support for integration
   - Tier C (1M+/mo commit): custom pricing (15–25% typical), dedicated capacity option on Dedicated plan, extended SLA, and credits negotiated per deal

Operational notes:
- Credits are non-refundable but can be applied to usage (tokens/embeds).
- Pilot credits conversion requires signing the MSA and an amendment that references the commit and credit conversion clause.
- Standard procurement path: MSA (2–4 business days review for standard customers) -> SOW (if you want professional services) -> DocuSign. Rishi can accelerate with our legal team if needed.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (token examples, numeric scenarios), sample_msa_summary.txt

I’ll kick off a quick internal check on EU residency constraints for hosted models and confirm by COB today.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Thanks Marta & Soojin — quick follow-up with a couple of practical examples to make the decision easier.

Example A (bursty generation):
- Pilot: 120k tokens used (est).
- If you choose pilot-only and then run at public hosted rates: $0.0005/token -> ~$60 for that pilot volume.
- If you convert pilot credits under the 6-month 100k/mo commit (Tier A): effective first-month delta is one-time credit applied; your blended effective token price in month 1 could be ~ $0.00045/token assuming typical credit usage.

Example B (embedding-heavy nightly jobs):
- Monthly embed volume: 20M embed units (example). With Tier B commit (300k/mo) and 12% discount + 500k onboarding credits, we can recommend a quantization profile and batching config to reduce unit cost further — we’ll include expected throughput and a conservative cost-estimate in the SOW.

Pilot governance & deliverables we propose:
- Joint POC plan with 3 success metrics (latency < 200ms p95, embed recall >= baseline, cost per embed target)
- Credit release: we can front-load up to 120k tokens; if you sign commit, up to 80% unused convert back as described.

Next steps: I can prepare a short SOW and a one-page legal amendment that encodes the credit conversion. If you want a binding pricing schedule we’ll include it in the MSA exhibit.

Also: attaching a sample SOW template and our pricing matrix.
